macro.note: Confirmed on EIA's own page as the next release. Prior week crude +0.1 mmbbl to 428.9 mmbbl, 1% above the five-year average; refinery utilization 97.4%. Matters more than usual with Hormuz transit volumes down to four vessels Tuesday against a ten-day average near thirteen.

Confirmed on the Federal Reserve Board's own September 2026 calendar. Last Beige Book before the September 15-16 FOMC, and the first since the hawkish repricing began - the inflation and pricing-power anecdotes are the section to read given ISM prices paid held at 71.1.
Prior 33,429 cuts in July, down 27% and the lowest monthly total in two years. Time confirmed on Challenger's own release calendar - note several aggregators wrongly list 9:30 AM.

Prior 203,000, down from an upwardly revised 207,000, per the Labor Department's own release. Do not pair this with the 227K figure circulating as consensus - that is a Trading Economics model output, not a survey. Claims are a DOL release, not BLS.

macro.event: International Trade in Goods and Services, July
macro.note: Date confirmed on BEA's own schedule. The published Census advance estimate showed the GOODS deficit ballooning to $118.8bn from $101.4bn, exports -$6.0bn and imports +$11.4bn - the widest goods gap since March 2025. Sets up a sharply wider total deficit and a negative Q3 net-exports contribution.

Confirmed on the BLS September calendar. Preliminary Q2 was productivity +1.4% annualized and unit labor costs +1.3%, well above consensus at the time. Productivity is the variable that decides whether the AI capital-spending boom is disinflationary or not - directly relevant to the hike debate.

macro.event: Fed Governor Waller, Economic Outlook (Reuters NEXT, virtual)
macro.note: Confirmed by raw-HTML inspection of the Federal Reserve Board's own September calendar, which lists only two Board speeches for the entire month - Barr on the 1st and Waller on the 3rd. The date-and-speaker pairing was verified cell by cell because the Fed's layout places the date column far from the speaker name and extraction tools transpose them. Waller speaks at the same minute as claims, trade and productivity.

Confirmed on the Cleveland Fed's own president's page. Important qualification: the issuer describes this as OPENING REMARKS at a community-development webinar, not a policy speech - do not brief it as a policy signal. Context that makes it interesting anyway: Hammack dissented in favor of RAISING the funds rate at the July FOMC.

The week's main event. Prior -23,000 against a twelve-month average of +34,000, with May and June revised down a combined 103,000. Honest range +50K to +90K, clustered +55K to +65K. Wolfe at +65K and 4.16%; PNC cites consensus +60K and 4.2%; Capital Economics +90K but with an internally inconsistent u-rate. Largest dispersion is average hourly earnings: Wolfe +0.35% m/m against consensus near +0.2%, the most likely hawkish surprise. The Goldman '+60K, 4.3%' forecast circulating widely is a stale 2025 artifact - do not quote it.

macro.event: Labor Day - US equity and bond markets closed
macro.note: Confirmed on both the Nasdaq trader holiday calendar and the Fed's own September calendar, which notes daily and weekly statistical releases scheduled for the 7th move to Tuesday the 8th.

Confirmed unamended on Finance Canada's own page. Tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on roughly 700 US product lines covering $27.6bn of imports, matching US Section 338 and 232 tariffs dollar for dollar. Sectors: steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics. Goods in transit on the effective date are exempt - the one operationally useful detail for modelling the impact.

Two-day meeting hosted by the Deutsche Bundesbank in Berlin, not Frankfurt, per the ECB's own calendar. Deposit facility rate currently 2.25%, effective 17 June 2026 - the 2.00% figure still widely circulated is stale by more than a year. Markets now price a near-40% chance of a 3% deposit rate by March 2027, up from 25% a week ago.

macro.event: ECB rate decision and press conference (Berlin)
macro.note: Day 2 of the Berlin meeting, decision followed by press conference, per the ECB's own calendar. Time shown is indicative. The market is now carrying a live ECB tightening path for the first time this cycle.

Confirmed on the BLS September calendar, alongside Real Earnings at the same time. Critical sequencing: August CPI lands three business days BEFORE the FOMC decision, so the Committee will have both August inflation prints and Friday's payrolls in hand when it meets.

Statement 2:00 PM and press conference 2:30 PM on the 16th, confirmed at two Federal Reserve pages. CME's own FedWatch data as of Tuesday's close prices a 69% chance of a 25bp HIKE and zero chance of a cut. Blackout period began Saturday September 5.

earnings.note: Broadcom Q3 FY26 - the day's main single-stock event, confirmed on Broadcom's own investor site. Company guidance is roughly $29.4bn revenue, up 84% y/y, with $16.0bn from AI semiconductors - which would be about 54% of sales and the first quarter in which AI is a MAJORITY of Broadcom's revenue. Street consensus clusters at non-GAAP EPS $3.22 and revenue $29.24bn. Last quarter was $22.2bn revenue and $10.8bn of AI. The catch: when Broadcom first guided to $16bn, that figure landed roughly seven percentage points BELOW sell-side expectations near $17bn, so simply hitting it may not be enough. Watch custom XPU accelerator commentary, hyperscaler customer count, and Q4 AI guidance.
